title: Tap a closed door's bottom hinge pin up with a nail set and hammer, clear of the casing, then pull it out
instruction: Take the pin out of this door's bottom hinge.
context: Taking a door off to move furniture, paint or plane it starts here. Family Handyman: 'With the door closed and latched, remove the hinge pins by tapping on the bottom of the hinge pin with a nail and hammer.' The barrel sits against the door casing, so the hammer has little room: a hinge-pin-tool patent notes 'It is also easy to miss the nail and strike the molding around the doorframe, or even strike the door itself.'
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table, which is the floor. A painted drywall partition (fixed, 11.4 cm thick) faces the robot, its face at x 47.0, with a 30 x 80 in. opening whose hinge jamb is at y 0.2 to 1.9. In it, closed and latched, a 30 x 80 x 1-3/8 in. (76.2 x 203.2 x 3.5 cm) hollow-core flush door, white, 1.27 cm above the floor, y -76.4 to -0.16, hung on three 3-1/2 x 3-1/2 in. five-knuckle steel butt hinges (0.085 in. leaves, 0.234 in. loose pins with button tips). Bottom hinge (the only one in reach): barrel 1.08 cm across, axis at x 45.41, y 0.0, from 29.21 to 38.10 cm up. Pine casing 2-1/4 x 11/16 in. (5.7 x 1.75 cm), white, 3/16 in. reveal: hinge-side casing y 0.64 to 6.36, face at x 45.25. Baseboard 3-1/2 x 1/2 in. along the wall. Pin: steel, 5.94 mm x 88.9 mm with a 10.8 x 4.8 mm button head, 23 g, its lower end flush with the bottom knuckle's underside, head down on the top knuckle; painted in. Nail set (3/32 in., 10.2 cm, 9.5 mm knurled steel body tapering over 2.5 cm to a 2.4 mm cupped tip, 50 g) on the floor, tip toward the hinge at (30.5, -12.6), head at (23.2, -19.8). Claw hammer (16 oz, 30.4 cm, steel head 10.4 cm, wood handle, 0.567 kg) on its side, handle near the head at (21.5, 21.5), face toward x, handle running to (14, 44). Distractors (loose; scoring ignores them): a multi-purpose oil can 5.2 x 10.4 x 27.2 cm, 0.40 kg, at (40, -33); a retractable utility knife 16 x 6 cm, 0.12 kg, at (40, 36).
scoring: r is how far the pin's head stands above the top knuckle. Any part of the hammer touching the door, casing, wall, baseboard or hinge while moving at 0.10 m/s or more is a blow on the door or its trim, recorded for the rest of the run, and caps the score at 0.25. 1.0: the pin out of the hinge and lying on the floor (its middle within 12 mm of it), at least 3 cm from the hinge's axis, at rest, both grippers' fingertips at least 5 cm from it, and no blow on the door or trim, held 3 s. 0.75: the pin out of all five knuckles (its lower end at least 2 mm above the top knuckle, or its middle at least 15 mm off the hinge's axis). 0.5: r at least 30 mm. 0.25: r at least 4 mm (the pin broken loose). 0: otherwise; doing nothing leaves r at 0.
reset_notes: Push the pin back down until its head sits on the top knuckle and re-paint the seam (or use the reusable bound-pin stand-in in the README). Lay the nail set and hammer back on their tape marks.
fidelity: Wall, door, trim and hinge at full size; the table is the floor. The door is fixed (latched, on two more hinges). Until driven up 4 mm the pin is held in place and moves only by blows through the nail set (E = mv^2/2 of the hammer over a 60 N bond); then it is a rigid body pressed 2 N toward the jamb. Damage = hammer touching door/trim/hinge at >= 0.1 m/s. Nail set and doorway are custom meshes; hammer is SimReady. Uniform friction, no force sensing.
